subject: snail
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact, rigged snail model based on garden snail proportions, sketching out a spine skeleton running from tail to head along the ground.

For the skeleton structure, I'm working out a root joint near the body center with separate chains branching toward the tail and toward the head, so the full body path can be swept with varying radii to form the shell-to-foot taper.

Now I'm mapping out the body curve itself: a tapered path running from a thin tail tip, through a thicker core, up into a raised neck and head, with an elliptical radius profile (narrower at the tail, wider through the middle, rising at the head) to shape the creature's silhouette.

Still tuning the radius curve...

Checking the tube radius against the coil radius shrinkage, with whorls spaced so adjacent coils overlap slightly for a solid shell look, and using pitch along the axis to give it a conical lean over 2.5 turns.

Working out the shell's total extent and where to anchor its center so it sits plausibly against the body—checking that the bottom buries slightly into the body while the top doesn't overshoot the head height, then placing the aperture at the front-bottom.

I'm computing the X-axis rotation to figure out which direction the aperture starts moving (toward -Z initially based on the rotation matrix).

So the aperture opens forward at the shell start, opposite the tangent direction. I'll add a small lip there using a disc and torus shape for the opening, colored to match the body with a cream rim, then move on to painting spiral stripe bands along the tube.

Naming the tail chain, then planning the eye stalks and oral tentacles as sprouted chains off the head joint, positioning their base points relative to the head's local coordinates near the front of the body.

Testing a few candidate placements for the aperture, I find one where it faces up-forward which seems off for a realistic snail, so I try shifting "from" directly below the shell's center instead, which gives a tangent facing straight forward -- that puts the mouth right at the body's back where it can sit naturally on top without clipping through. I'm adding a small torus as the lip rim of the aperture opening to finish the shell mouth detail.
